name: Power Consumption Calculation
problem_statement: Tom is interested in power consumption of his favourite laptop. His laptop has three modes. In normal mode laptop consumes P1 watt per minute. T1 minutes after Tom moved the mouse or touched the keyboard for the last time, a screensaver starts and power consumption changes to P2 watt per minute. Finally, after T2 minutes from the start of the screensaver, laptop switches to the "sleep" mode and consumes P3 watt per minute. If Tom moves the mouse or touches the keyboard when the laptop is in the second or in the third mode, it switches to the first (normal) mode. Tom's work with the laptop can be divided into n time periods [l1, r1], [l2, r2], ..., [ln, rn]. During each interval Tom continuously moves the mouse and presses buttons on the keyboard. Between the periods Tom stays away from the laptop. Find out the total amount of power consumed by the laptop during the period [l1, rn].
input_specification: The first line contains 6 integer numbers n, P1, P2, P3, T1, T2 (1 ≤ n ≤ 100, 0 ≤ P1, P2, P3 ≤ 100, 1 ≤ T1, T2 ≤ 60). The following n lines contain description of Tom's work. Each i-th of these lines contains two space-separated integers li and ri (0 ≤ li < ri ≤ 1440, ri < li + 1 for i <  n), which stand for the start and the end of the i-th period of work.
output_specification: Output the answer to the problem.

sample_cases.title: First sample case from problem description
sample_cases.why_included: This is the first example from the problem statement. With n=1, there are no idle periods to calculate.

sample_cases.title: Second sample case from problem description
sample_cases.why_included: This is the second example. It tests an idle period that is long enough to enter all three power modes (P1, P2, P3).

sample_cases.title: Idle period shorter than T1
sample_cases.why_included: Tests an idle period (duration 5) that is shorter than T1 (20). The laptop stays in P1 mode during this gap.

sample_cases.title: Idle period exactly equal to T1
sample_cases.why_included: Tests the boundary where the idle period duration (10) is exactly T1. The laptop should stay in P1 mode for the whole gap.

sample_cases.title: Idle period enters P2 mode slightly
sample_cases.why_included: Tests the boundary where idle duration (11) is T1+1. This triggers exactly 1 minute of P2 (screensaver) mode.

sample_cases.title: Idle period shorter than T1+T2
sample_cases.why_included: Tests an idle period (duration 15) that is between T1 and T1+T2. The laptop enters P1 and P2 modes during the gap.

sample_cases.title: Idle period exactly equal to T1+T2
sample_cases.why_included: Tests the boundary where idle duration (30) is exactly T1+T2. The laptop should use P1 and P2 modes, but not enter P3 sleep mode.

sample_cases.title: Idle period enters P3 mode slightly
sample_cases.why_included: Tests the boundary where idle duration (31) is T1+T2+1. This triggers exactly 1 minute of P3 (sleep) mode.

sample_cases.title: Minimum values for all parameters
sample_cases.why_included: Tests with n=1 and all power consumptions at their minimum (0). The result must be 0.

sample_cases.title: Maximum values for all parameters
sample_cases.why_included: Stress test with maximum n, max power values, and many short intervals with short gaps. The gaps are all length 2, well within P1 range.

sample_cases.title: All power consumptions are equal
sample_cases.why_included: When all P values are the same, the total consumption is simply the total duration (r_n - l_1) times the power, regardless of modes.

sample_cases.title: Atypical power consumption P1 < P2 < P3
sample_cases.why_included: Tests an unusual but valid case where power consumption increases in screensaver/sleep modes. This shouldn't affect the logic.

sample_cases.title: Multiple gaps with different mode triggers
sample_cases.why_included: Tests a sequence of gaps: gap 1 is <T1 (P1 only), gap 2 is >T1 and <T1+T2 (P1, P2), gap 3 is >T1+T2 (P1, P2, P3).
